/-!
# Conjecture 3.45

by B. I. Plotkin

Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a hereditary radical. Is it true that, in a locally nilpotent
torsion-free group $G$, the subgroup $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ is isolated?

A radical in the sense of Kurosh and Plotkin is determined by its *radical class*
$\mathfrak{X}$ of groups. A class of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ is a radical class if it is closed
under homomorphic images, every group $G$ has a largest normal $\mathfrak{X}$-subgroup
$\mathfrak{X}(G)$ (the $\mathfrak{X}$-radical of $G$), and $\mathfrak{X}(G/\mathfrak{X}(G)) = 1$.
The radical is *hereditary* if $\mathfrak{X}$ is closed under taking subgroups; equivalently,
$H \cap \mathfrak{X}(G) \le \mathfrak{X}(H)$ for every subgroup $H$ of every group $G$.

A group is *locally nilpotent* if all its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent, and
*torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is
*isolated* if $g^n \in H$ for some $n \ge 1$ implies $g \in H$; this is `Subgroup.Saturated`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

abbrev GroupClass : Type (u + 1) := ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop

blocks.code:
def radical (G : Type u) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ 𝔛 N}
blocks.docstring:
The `𝔛`-radical `𝔛(G)` of a group `G`: the join of all normal subgroups of `G` that belong
to the class `𝔛`. For a radical class `𝔛` this is the largest normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib: only ring-theoretic radicals (Ideal.radical, nilradical, Jacobson) and Koethe radical in the repo; no group-class radical.
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.45».radical
justification.why_needed: The 𝔛-radical 𝔛(G) = sSup of all normal 𝔛-subgroups of G; the object the problem asks about. Comes with a (fully proven) `Normal` instance so that `G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G` makes sense.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_radical {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (hN : 𝔛 N) :
    N ≤ radical 𝔛 G :=
  le_sSup ⟨‹N.Normal›, hN⟩
blocks.docstring: Every normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G` is contained in the `𝔛`-radical of `G`.
blocks.name: le_radical
blocks.text:
/-- Every normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G` is contained in the `𝔛`-radical of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_radical {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (hN : 𝔛 N) :
    N ≤ radical 𝔛 G :=
  le_sSup ⟨‹N.Normal›, hN⟩

blocks.code:
instance radical_normal (G : Type u) [Group G] : (radical 𝔛 G).Normal := by
  have h : (radical 𝔛 G).normalCore = radical 𝔛 G :=
    le_antisymm (Subgroup.normalCore_le _) <| sSup_le fun N hN =>
      haveI := hN.1
      Subgroup.normal_le_normalCore.mpr (le_sSup hN)
  exact h ▸ Subgroup.normalCore_normal _
blocks.docstring: The `𝔛`-radical of `G` is a normal subgroup of `G`.
blocks.name: radical_normal
blocks.text:
/-- The `𝔛`-radical of `G` is a normal subgroup of `G`. -/
instance radical_normal (G : Type u) [Group G] : (radical 𝔛 G).Normal := by
  have h : (radical 𝔛 G).normalCore = radical 𝔛 G :=
    le_antisymm (Subgroup.normalCore_le _) <| sSup_le fun N hN =>
      haveI := hN.1
      Subgroup.normal_le_normalCore.mpr (le_sSup hN)
  exact h ▸ Subgroup.normalCore_normal _

blocks.code:
structure IsRadicalClass : Prop where
  /-- `𝔛` is closed under homomorphic images. -/
  of_surjective {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    𝔛 G → 𝔛 H
  /-- The join of all normal `𝔛`-subgroups of `G` is an `𝔛`-group. -/
  radical_mem (G : Type u) [Group G] : 𝔛 (radical 𝔛 G)
  /-- `𝔛(G ⧸ 𝔛(G)) = 1`. -/
  radical_quotient (G : Type u) [Group G] : radical 𝔛 (G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G) = ⊥
blocks.docstring:
A class of groups `𝔛` is a *radical class* (Kurosh) if
* `𝔛` is closed under homomorphic images (in particular under isomorphisms),
* for every group `G` the join `𝔛(G)` of all normal `𝔛`-subgroups of `G` is again an `𝔛`-group,
  so that `𝔛(G)` is the largest normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G`, and
* the `𝔛`-radical of `G ⧸ 𝔛(G)` is trivial.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No Mathlib/repo notion of Kurosh–Amitsur radical classes of groups exists. The equivalent Q/E/N-closure characterization (Robinson) was considered; Kurosh's original three axioms were chosen as closer to the source's framework.
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.45».IsRadicalClass
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's definition of a radical class: closed under homomorphic images (surjective homs, which also gives isomorphism-invariance), the join of all normal 𝔛-subgroups of any G is an 𝔛-group (so it is the largest normal 𝔛-subgroup), and radical 𝔛 (G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G) = ⊥.

blocks.name: IsRadicalClass
blocks.text:
/-- A class of groups `𝔛` is a *radical class* (Kurosh) if
* `𝔛` is closed under homomorphic images (in particular under isomorphisms),
* for every group `G` the join `𝔛(G)` of all normal `𝔛`-subgroups of `G` is again an `𝔛`-group,
  so that `𝔛(G)` is the largest normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G`, and
* the `𝔛`-radical of `G ⧸ 𝔛(G)` is trivial. -/
structure IsRadicalClass : Prop where
  /-- `𝔛` is closed under homomorphic images. -/
  of_surjective {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    𝔛 G → 𝔛 H
  /-- The join of all normal `𝔛`-subgroups of `G` is an `𝔛`-group. -/
  radical_mem (G : Type u) [Group G] : 𝔛 (radical 𝔛 G)
  /-- `𝔛(G ⧸ 𝔛(G)) = 1`. -/
  radical_quotient (G : Type u) [Group G] : radical 𝔛 (G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G) = ⊥

structure IsHereditaryRadicalClass : Prop extends IsRadicalClass 𝔛 where
  /-- `𝔛` is closed under subgroups. -/
  of_subgroup (G : Type u) [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) : 𝔛 G → 𝔛 H
blocks.docstring: A radical class `𝔛` is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking subgroups.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or the repo.
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.45».IsHereditaryRadicalClass
justification.why_needed: Hereditary radical = radical class closed under taking subgroups (as fixed by the decomposition table; equivalent to H ∩ 𝔛(G) ≤ 𝔛(H) for all H ≤ G).

  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isHereditaryRadicalClass_top : IsHereditaryRadicalClass (fun _ _ => True) where
  of_surjective _ _ _ := trivial
  radical_mem _ := trivial
  radical_quotient G := by
    refine (Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall _).mpr fun x _ => ?_
    induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
    | H g => exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff g).mpr (by rw [radical_top]; exact Subgroup.mem_top g)
  of_subgroup _ _ _ _ := trivial
blocks.docstring: The class of all groups is a hereditary radical class.

  radical_mem _ := trivial
  radical_quotient G := by

    induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
    | H g => exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff g).mpr (by rw [radical_top]; exact Subgroup.mem_top g)
  of_subgroup _ _ _ _ := trivial

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, implicitly universally quantified over all hereditary radicals 𝔛 (in the Kurosh–Amitsur/Plotkin sense for groups: a radical class closed under subgroups) and all locally nilpotent torsion-free groups G; 'isolated' means the subgroup 𝔛(G) is closed under taking roots (g^n ∈ 𝔛(G) with n ≥ 1 implies g ∈ 𝔛(G)); the notion of 'hereditary radical' is not a Mathlib primitive and must be defined explicitly.
claims.reviewer_why: c05's declaration is used as the base (Kurosh radical class as a Prop-structure: Q-closed, the join 𝔛(G) of normal 𝔛-subgroups lies in 𝔛, 𝔛(G/𝔛(G)) = ⊥; hereditary = subgroup-closed; locally nilpotent = every f.g. subgroup nilpotent; torsion-free stated literally as ∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1; universe-polymorphic class of groups; fully proven API/test lemmas). Edits: 'isolated' is now Mathlib's `Subgroup.Saturated` (as in c03/c04; exactly g^n ∈ H → n = 0 ∨ g ∈ H) instead of a bespoke `IsIsolated`, the bespoke-`IsIsolated` test lemma was therefore dropped, and c04/c06's `le_radical` API lemma and `IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent` test were added. c01/c03/c04 are equally faithful modulo using `IsMulTorsionFree` (unique roots), which is a priori stronger than torsion-free for non-abelian groups and coincides with it under local nilpotency only via Mal'cev's theorem; the literal form avoids that dependence. c06 (Q/N/E closure) and c02/c07 ('no nontrivial normal 𝔛-subgroup of the quotient') are equivalent but less standard/less readable encodings. c08 was rejected: its `IsHereditaryRadical` omits the semisimplicity axiom 𝔛(G/𝔛(G)) = 1, so it also quantifies over non-radical classes such as the class of locally nilpotent groups (not extension-closed: S₃), i.e. a strictly stronger universal statement.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.45

by B. I. Plotkin

Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a hereditary radical. Is it true that, in a locally nilpotent
torsion-free group $G$, the subgroup $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ is isolated?

A radical in the sense of Kurosh and Plotkin is determined by its *radical class*
$\mathfrak{X}$ of groups. A class of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ is a radical class if it is closed
under homomorphic images, every group $G$ has a largest normal $\mathfrak{X}$-subgroup
$\mathfrak{X}(G)$ (the $\mathfrak{X}$-radical of $G$), and $\mathfrak{X}(G/\mathfrak{X}(G)) = 1$.
The radical is *hereditary* if $\mathfrak{X}$ is closed under taking subgroups; equivalently,
$H \cap \mathfrak{X}(G) \le \mathfrak{X}(H)$ for every subgroup $H$ of every group $G$.

A group is *locally nilpotent* if all its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent, and
*torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is
*isolated* if $g^n \in H$ for some $n \ge 1$ implies $g \in H$; this is `Subgroup.Saturated`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«3.45»

/-- A class of groups, given as a predicate on groups in `Type u`. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type (u + 1) := ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop

variable (𝔛 : GroupClass.{u})

/-- The `𝔛`-radical `𝔛(G)` of a group `G`: the join of all normal subgroups of `G` that belong
to the class `𝔛`. For a radical class `𝔛` this is the largest normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G`. -/
def radical (G : Type u) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ 𝔛 N}

/-- Every normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G` is contained in the `𝔛`-radical of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_radical {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (hN : 𝔛 N) :
    N ≤ radical 𝔛 G :=
  le_sSup ⟨‹N.Normal›, hN⟩

/-- The `𝔛`-radical of `G` is a normal subgroup of `G`. -/
instance radical_normal (G : Type u) [Group G] : (radical 𝔛 G).Normal := by
  have h : (radical 𝔛 G).normalCore = radical 𝔛 G :=
    le_antisymm (Subgroup.normalCore_le _) <| sSup_le fun N hN =>
      haveI := hN.1
      Subgroup.normal_le_normalCore.mpr (le_sSup hN)
  exact h ▸ Subgroup.normalCore_normal _

/-- A class of groups `𝔛` is a *radical class* (Kurosh) if
* `𝔛` is closed under homomorphic images (in particular under isomorphisms),
* for every group `G` the join `𝔛(G)` of all normal `𝔛`-subgroups of `G` is again an `𝔛`-group,
  so that `𝔛(G)` is the largest normal `𝔛`-subgroup of `G`, and
* the `𝔛`-radical of `G ⧸ 𝔛(G)` is trivial. -/
structure IsRadicalClass : Prop where
  /-- `𝔛` is closed under homomorphic images. -/
  of_surjective {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    𝔛 G → 𝔛 H
  /-- The join of all normal `𝔛`-subgroups of `G` is an `𝔛`-group. -/
  radical_mem (G : Type u) [Group G] : 𝔛 (radical 𝔛 G)
  /-- `𝔛(G ⧸ 𝔛(G)) = 1`. -/
  radical_quotient (G : Type u) [Group G] : radical 𝔛 (G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G) = ⊥

/-- A radical class `𝔛` is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking subgroups. -/
structure IsHereditaryRadicalClass : Prop extends IsRadicalClass 𝔛 where
  /-- `𝔛` is closed under subgroups. -/
  of_subgroup (G : Type u) [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) : 𝔛 G → 𝔛 H

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- Nilpotent groups are locally nilpotent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- The radical of the class of all groups is the whole group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem radical_top (G : Type u) [Group G] : radical (fun _ _ => True) G = ⊤ :=
  top_le_iff.mp (le_radical _ ⊤ trivial)

/-- The class of all groups is a hereditary radical class. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isHereditaryRadicalClass_top : IsHereditaryRadicalClass (fun _ _ => True) where
  of_surjective _ _ _ := trivial
  radical_mem _ := trivial
  radical_quotient G := by
    refine (Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall _).mpr fun x _ => ?_
    induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
    | H g => exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff g).mpr (by rw [radical_top]; exact Subgroup.mem_top g)
  of_subgroup _ _ _ _ := trivial

/--
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a hereditary radical. Is it true that, in a locally nilpotent
torsion-free group $G$, the subgroup $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ is isolated?

Here $\mathfrak{X}$ ranges over all hereditary radical classes of groups, $\mathfrak{X}(G)$ is
the $\mathfrak{X}$-radical of $G$ (its largest normal $\mathfrak{X}$-subgroup), "torsion-free"
means that no element other than $1$ has finite order, and "isolated" means that
$g^n \in \mathfrak{X}(G)$ with $n \geq 1$ implies $g \in \mathfrak{X}(G)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.45» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (𝔛 : GroupClass.{u}), IsHereditaryRadicalClass 𝔛 →
      ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], IsLocallyNilpotent G → (∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) →
        (radical 𝔛 G).Saturated := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.45»

items: 'Hereditary radical' is formalized, per the decomposition table, as a Kurosh radical class closed under all subgroups (Plotkin's sense for groups). The ring-theoretic analogue 'closed under normal subgroups/ideals' was not used; reviewers should confirm this reading matches Plotkin's usage.

Radical class uses Kurosh's three axioms with 𝔛(G) := sSup of normal 𝔛-subgroups: (i) closed under surjective homomorphisms (implies isomorphism-closure), (ii) 𝔛 (radical 𝔛 G) (equivalent to 'G has a largest normal 𝔛-subgroup'), (iii) radical 𝔛 (G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G) = ⊥. This is equivalent to the Q-, E-, N-closure characterization. The empty class is excluded by (ii), as in Kurosh.
Classes of groups are predicates on groups in a fixed universe `Type u`; the theorem is universe-polymorphic. This is the standard way to model a proper class of groups.

Torsion-free is stated literally as `∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1` rather than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injectivity of x ↦ x^n), which for non-abelian groups is a priori stronger (e.g. the Klein bottle group). Under local nilpotency the two are equivalent by Mal'cev's unique-roots theorem, but the literal form avoids relying on that theorem. Note the repo's Kaplansky.lean uses `IsMulTorsionFree`.
Isolated: `∀ g n, 0 < n → g ^ n ∈ H → g ∈ H` (n = 0 is excluded since g^0 = 1 ∈ H always).
Locally nilpotent: every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent (`Subgroup.FG` + `Group.IsNilpotent ↥H`).

Additional API/test declarations (radical_top, isHereditaryRadicalClass_top, isIsolated_bot) are fully proven and sanity-check the definitions: the class of all groups is a hereditary radical class with radical ⊤, and ⊥ is isolated in torsion-free groups.

reviewer_notes: Interpretive points a human should confirm: (1) 'Hereditary radical' is read, per the decomposition table and Russian usage (наследственный класс = subgroup-closed, cf. hereditary formations), as a Kurosh radical class closed under ALL subgroups (equivalently H ∩ 𝔛(G) ≤ 𝔛(H) for all H ≤ G). The ring-theoretic analogue 'closed under normal subgroups only' would quantify over more radicals and give a formally different statement; several candidates flagged this too. Under the subgroup-closed reading, Plotkin's more general functorial radicals coincide with Kurosh radicals (hereditary forces ρ(ρ(G)) = ρ(G)), so no generality is lost by modelling the radical by its radical class. (2) 'Torsion-free' is stated literally (only 1 has finite order) rather than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injective power maps); the two agree for locally nilpotent groups by Mal'cev's unique-roots theorem, so either is faithful, but the literal form does not rely on that theorem. (3) The statement is universe-polymorphic (classes of groups in Type u); other Kourovka files fix Type, but both are accepted in the repo (cf. ErdosProblems/74). Sanity: the class of all groups (𝔛(G) = G) and of trivial groups (𝔛(G) = 1, saturated in torsion-free G) are hereditary radical classes, so the hypotheses are satisfiable and the answer is not forced by degenerate cases.
